docs.title: Review of Petite Provence Boulangerie & Patisserie
docs.text:
Google review of Petite Provence Boulangerie & Patisserie (5 out of 5, by James ST, 2 months ago): If you’re looking for a brunch spot with a cozy atmosphere and a menu that’s a little different from the usual, this place is definitely worth checking out.

One thing that stood out was the risotto cakes, not something you come across very often. They were crispy on the outside, creamy inside, and paired with perfectly poached eggs. The eggs themselves were good, though the risotto cakes were definitely the highlight of the dish.

The Northwest salmon hash was solid. It was flavorful and satisfying, although it wasn’t particularly memorable compared to the more unique items on the menu.

The croissant was excellent—light, buttery, and wonderfully flaky. It came with a berry jam that was sweet without being overpowering, making for a simple but delicious combination.

The freshly squeezed orange juice was another standout. You can immediately tell it’s made fresh, with a bright, natural citrus flavor that’s a huge step above typical commercial orange juice.

Beyond the food, the staff were friendly and welcoming, and the cafe has a warm, charming French bakery vibe. They also have an in-house pastry selection, which is worth browsing before you leave.

Overall, it’s a great brunch spot if you’re looking for quality food, fresh ingredients, and a relaxed atmosphere. I’d definitely come back to try more of their unique menu items and pastries.

docs.text:
Google review of Podnah's BBQ (5 out of 5, by Tom Everman, 4 months ago): I went on a “BBQ CRAWL” with a group of nine guys tonight. We hit three of Portland’s best “pits”. Each deserved a glowing review, and when it comes to real Texas BBQ I am tough to impress.

Podnah’s was one of the best barbecue places I’ve been to in a long time. The brisket was smoky, tender, and packed with flavor without trying too hard. We shared a huge beef rib that was tasty, juicy moist and the meat fell off the bone it was so tender. I also had a fabulously juicy Smoked Link.

The sides were just as good, if not better,  especially the Texas caviar — a cold mix of black-eyed peas, crunchy vegetables, and tangy dressing that went great with the rich barbecue. I also had the Green Chili Mac and Cheese with the perfect blend of creamy cheese with just the right bite.

Everything felt relaxed, friendly, and real. You can tell the people there care about making honest food that tastes great. I’m coming back just as soon as I can.

docs.text: Google review of Great Notion Brewing - Alberta (3 out of 5, by Garrett Drake, 11 months ago): We stopped here for a flight of their sours, but they were actually tart ales, which isn’t exactly what I had expected.  It was difficult to find since it seems the only street sign is surrounded by trees.  The tart ales were pretty good, but my girlfriend only liked the boo berry muffin and the key lime fluff.  The flight was pretty pricey though, $19 for 25oz vs $6-9 for a 16oz pint.  It’s a pretty open space with a good number of tables and a pretty large bar.  The food was order from a window on one side of the building.  The tables are encouraged for online ordering and paying, which I didn’t enjoy.  I’d rather order from a real menu with a real person.  The drinks were delivered by a bartender though and from what I saw at other tables the food is delivered as well. Overall, it wasn’t a bad experience, but it wasn’t good either and I won’t be returning.

Google review of Bollywood Theater (1 out of 5, by Ankit Bhatnagar, 2 months ago): Massive downgrade since 2021 -
What used to be a fun spot for street food has turned into a bland, westernized shadow of itself. We ordered some things we had before but almost everything missed the mark. The aloo tikki was two massive, thick slabs of dry potato without crispiness or spice, and the paneer makhani was way too tangy and not flavorful. The papad was served room temp—decent, but nothing special—leaving a simple yellow dal as literally the only good item of the meal. docs.title: Review of Abraham's Fabric Clinic
docs.text:
Google review of Abraham's Fabric Clinic (1 out of 5, by C H, 2 years ago): I've been a customer here for as long as I've lived in Portland. Abraham was absolutely amazing, which made sense considering he used to tailor suits for Johnny Carson in LA. I was so grateful to have such a gem of a person and business in my neighborhood!

Unfortunately, things have changed. I don't know if Abraham has retired, but it's been a year or two since I've seen him. I first really noticed his absence when I had a button and a clasp re-sewn on some pants some time ago. I was surprised when I got them home and actually looked at the button, which was technically attached, but literally dangling off. Life was busy then, I considered it a fluke, and didn't make a fuss.

Even more unfortunately, I recently entrusted another minor fix to the seamstress at Abraham's. A zipper on some of my favorite, professional slacks had gone off the rails. I took the pants in to ask if there were some way to just realign the zipper teeth. I was told the zipper would be fixed and paid $25 up front. I was nervous but thought again that maybe the previous bad work was an anomaly.

It was not an anomaly and culminated in shockingly bad experience.

When I went in to pick up the pants, I was sure to take a look while there. Immediately I saw that the stitching below the button was messy and thick. I pointed it out and the seamstress and she said "Oh, I just didn't clean it up." and immediately began hacking at all the threads with shears. There was an exchange where she asked if I wanted her to redo it and I declined.

When I got the pants home and looked closer, I could see that the whole job was shoddy. All the seams throughout the repair are crooked and unsightly. The zipper is a rigid, heavy duty metal zipper which seems inappropriate for the garment. Worst of all when she was recklessly hacking at threads, she actually cut a hole in the fabric of the pants!

I decided to call in. The dry cleaning person answered, and I asked if he was the best person to receive a complaint. Without response he handed the phone to the seamstress. I said hello and that I'd just been there about the zipper and added that she had cut a hole in the fabric. I said I'd like to be refunded at the least, and ideally compensated for the pants.

She said, "The work was done." and hung up on me.

So that's that. Careless, shoddy work. Rude treatment. I will never take any of my clothing there again for any reason and I would not recommend them to anyone else.

They insisted my insurance (medi-cal) wouldn’t cover it (my insurance rep remarked “walgreens should know better”).  When i asked if they weren’t willing to fill out the form, they told me they WOULD fill out the form but wouldn’t fill my rx unless it was covered. I wasted days waiting to hear back from them, then i called my insurance and found out they’d they never faxed the form back.

It’s Walgreens choice if they won’t fill out forms but lying to me and dismissing my needs was uncalled for. Had they been honest about their refusal to work with my insurance, I would have saved a four day delay in getting my medicine while visiting family for a week. Thankfully i found Genoa Healthcare, whose pharmacy WAS willing to fill out the form so that my rx was covered by Medi-cal.

If you have a complex situation don’t waste your time with this pharmacy. I thought it would be easy for a national chain to transfer my pick up from my local walgreens to the nearest one, but it ended up being a hinderance to timely and professional care. I realize Walgreens might be so swamped that they don’t want to deal with forms, but they should at least be honest and up front about it.
